note.explanation: Metallic character describes how readily an element loses electrons. In a group, metallic character and reactivity generally increase downwards; across a period, metallic character decreases from left to right.
examples: Potassium is more metallic than sodium because potassium is lower in Group 1.
Sodium is more reactive than magnesium in Period 3, as your textbook explains.
note.checkAnswer: Metallic character and reactivity generally increase down a group.
note.simple: Metals tend to lose electrons. The easier an atom loses electrons, the more metallic it is.
note.checkQuestion: How does metallic character change down a group?
note.title: Metallic character and reactivity
steps: Remember that metallic character means the tendency to lose electrons and form positive ions.
Down a group, ionization energy decreases, so atoms lose electrons more easily.
Therefore metallic character and reactivity generally increase down a group.
From left to right in a period, the nucleus attracts valence electrons more strongly, so metallic character decreases.
note.answer: Metallic character and reactivity generally increase down a group. Metallic character decreases from left to right in a period.

options: It generally increases because atoms lose electrons more easily down the group.
It generally decreases because atoms gain more shells.
It stays the same because the elements are in one group.
It decreases because ionization energy decreases.
mcqs.stem: What happens to metallic character as you move down a group?
rationales: Correct: lower ionization energy down a group makes losing electrons easier.
Incorrect: gaining shells does not make metallic character decrease; the trend is generally an increase.
Incorrect: elements in a group have similar properties, but their metallic character still changes gradually down the group.
Incorrect: decreasing ionization energy makes electron loss easier, so metallic character increases.

options: It increases because nuclear attraction for valence electrons becomes stronger.
It decreases because increasing nuclear charge makes electron loss more difficult.
It stays constant because the elements are in one period.
It increases because the number of valence electrons decreases.
mcqs.stem: Why does metallic character generally decrease from left to right across a period?
rationales: Incorrect: stronger attraction makes it harder, not easier, to lose valence electrons.
Correct: increasing nuclear charge pulls valence electrons more strongly, making them harder to lose.
Incorrect: properties change across a period even though the elements are in the same period.
Incorrect: the number of valence electrons generally increases across a period.

options: Li
Na
K
Rb
mcqs.stem: Which of these Group 1 elements is expected to have the greatest metallic character?
rationales: Incorrect: lithium is highest in the list and has the least metallic character of these choices.
Incorrect: sodium is more metallic than lithium, but less metallic than the elements below it.
Incorrect: potassium is more metallic than lithium and sodium, but less metallic than rubidium.
Correct: metallic character generally increases down a group, and rubidium is lowest in this list.

options: Sodium is generally more reactive because it loses an electron more readily.
Magnesium is generally more reactive because it has more protons.
They have equal reactivity because they are in the same period.
Neither is reactive because both are metals.
mcqs.stem: According to the trend described for Period 3, which statement compares sodium and magnesium?
rationales: Correct: your textbook describes sodium as very reactive and magnesium as less reactive in this period.
Incorrect: more protons do not by themselves make magnesium lose electrons more readily across the period.
Incorrect: elements in the same period do not have equal reactivity.
Incorrect: metals can be reactive; the section uses sodium and magnesium as examples.

options: g/cm³
g/cm
cm³/g
g
mcqs.stem: In which unit does your textbook express density?
rationales: Correct: density is expressed in grams per cubic centimetre, g/cm³.
Incorrect: g/cm is not the unit given for density.
Incorrect: cm³/g is the inverse of a density unit.
Incorrect: grams alone measure mass, not density.

options: Density always decreases from top to bottom in every group.
Density generally increases from top to bottom in a group, but individual values may vary.
Density changes greatly from left to right in every period.
All elements in a group have equal densities.
mcqs.stem: Which statement best matches the density trend stated in this section?
rationales: Incorrect: the stated general trend is an increase down a group.
Correct: density generally increases down a group, though the table shows that individual values need not rise at every step.
Incorrect: your textbook says density varies less significantly from left to right in a period.
Incorrect: densities are not equal for all elements in a group.

options: A metal reacting with oxygen
A non-metal reacting with oxygen
Two noble gases reacting
Two metals combining without oxygen
mcqs.stem: Which combination is expected to produce a basic oxide?
rationales: Correct: a metal reacting with oxygen generally forms a basic oxide.
Incorrect: a non-metal reacting with oxygen generally forms an acidic oxide.
Incorrect: noble gases are generally unreactive and this is not the expected oxide-forming combination.
Incorrect: without oxygen, this does not describe the formation of an oxide.

options: Group 1
Group 2
Group 17
Group 18
mcqs.stem: Which group is associated with the most electropositive elements in the usual periodic trends?
rationales: Correct: Group 1 elements readily lose electrons and are highly electropositive.
Incorrect: Group 2 elements are electropositive, but Group 1 elements are generally the most electropositive.
Incorrect: Group 17 elements are highly electronegative, not the most electropositive.
Incorrect: Group 18 elements are generally unreactive noble gases.

written.text: Barium (Ba) is present in 2nd group and 6th period. Answer the following questions about this element. (i) Is it a metal or a non-metal? (ii) Will it be electropositive or electronegative? (iii) What is the nature of its oxide? (iv) In which physical state you expect this element to exist?

rubric.description: Identify its metallic and electrical character.
rubric.how: State that barium is a metal and is electropositive.

rubric.why: The nature of the oxide follows from barium being a metal.
rubric.description: Give the nature of its oxide.
rubric.how: State that its oxide is basic.

rubric.why: The question asks for the expected physical state at normal conditions.
rubric.description: Give its physical state.
rubric.how: State that barium is a solid.

rubric.why: The period indicates the element's expected shell level and supports locating it.
rubric.description: Use its stated position correctly.
rubric.how: Identify it as a Group 2, Period 6 metal.

modelAnswer: (ii) It is electropositive because it tends to lose electrons.
(iv) Barium is expected to exist as a solid.

written.text: In which group and period you expect to find an element with the largest atomic radius?

rubric.why: Atomic radius increases down a group, and Group 1 is at the left edge of the table.
rubric.description: Identify the group.
rubric.how: State Group 1.

rubric.why: Atomic radius increases down the table, so the bottom period is required.
rubric.description: Identify the period.
rubric.how: State Period 7.

modelAnswer: Atomic radius increases down a group and from right to left across a period.
Therefore, the element with the largest atomic radius is expected in Group 1, Period 7.

written.text: Can you predict the group number of the most electropositive and the most electronegative elements?
written.finalAnswer: Most electropositive: Group 1; most electronegative: Group 17.

rubric.why: Electropositive elements readily lose electrons; this character is greatest toward the lower left of the periodic table.
rubric.description: Give the group of the most electropositive elements.
rubric.how: State Group 1.

rubric.why: The most electronegative elements are toward the upper right among the reactive elements.
rubric.description: Give the group of the most electronegative elements.
rubric.how: State Group 17.

modelAnswer: The most electropositive elements are expected in Group 1.
The most electronegative elements are expected in Group 17.

written.text: Choose among the following the element having the lowest ionization energy and the element with highest electron affinity. Also assign its group number and period number Li, K, O, F, Cl.
written.finalAnswer: K has the lowest ionization energy (Group 1, Period 4); Cl has the highest electron affinity (Group 17, Period 3).

rubric.why: Ionization energy decreases down a group, making potassium the lowest among the listed choices.
rubric.description: Choose the element with the lowest ionization energy.
rubric.how: Select K.

rubric.why: The element's group and period complete the required location.
rubric.description: Locate K.
rubric.how: Give Group 1, Period 4.

rubric.why: Chlorine has the highest electron affinity among the listed choices.
rubric.description: Choose the element with the highest electron affinity.
rubric.how: Select Cl.

rubric.why: The element's group and period complete the required location.
rubric.description: Locate Cl.
rubric.how: Give Group 17, Period 3.

modelAnswer: Ionization energy decreases down a group; among the given elements, K has the lowest ionization energy.
Among the given elements, Cl has the highest electron affinity.

written.text: Which two elements of the periodic table react to give (i) A basic oxide and (ii) An acidic oxide?
written.finalAnswer: (i) A metal such as magnesium and oxygen give a basic oxide. (ii) A non-metal such as carbon and oxygen give an acidic oxide.

rubric.why: A metal and oxygen are the required reactants for a basic oxide.
rubric.description: Name the reactants for a basic oxide.
rubric.how: Give a metal and oxygen, for example magnesium and oxygen.

rubric.why: The product type must be identified correctly.
rubric.description: Identify the first product.
rubric.how: State that they form a basic oxide.

rubric.why: A non-metal and oxygen are the required reactants for an acidic oxide.
rubric.description: Name the reactants for an acidic oxide.
rubric.how: Give a non-metal and oxygen, for example carbon and oxygen.

rubric.why: The product type must be identified correctly.
rubric.description: Identify the second product.
rubric.how: State that they form an acidic oxide.

modelAnswer: (i) A metal such as magnesium reacts with oxygen to give a basic oxide.
(ii) A non-metal such as carbon reacts with oxygen to give an acidic oxide.

written.text: Do you expect calcium to be more reactive than sodium? Give the reason of your answer.
written.finalAnswer: No. Sodium is expected to be more reactive than calcium because sodium loses its outer electron more readily.

rubric.why: The response must make the correct comparison between the two metals.
rubric.description: Give the comparison.
rubric.how: State that calcium is not more reactive; sodium is more reactive.

rubric.why: A reason linked to electron loss explains the metallic reactivity comparison.
rubric.description: Explain the comparison.
rubric.how: Explain that sodium loses its outer electron more readily.

modelAnswer: No, calcium is not expected to be more reactive than sodium.
Sodium loses its outer electron more readily, so it is more reactive.

written.text: Which element has the least value of ionization energy and which element has the highest value of electronegativity?
written.finalAnswer: Francium has the least ionization energy; fluorine has the highest electronegativity.

rubric.why: Ionization energy generally decreases down a group, making the lower-left element the expected minimum.
rubric.description: Name the element with the least ionization energy.
rubric.how: State francium.

rubric.why: Electronegativity is greatest toward the upper right of the periodic table among the reactive elements.
rubric.description: Name the element with the highest electronegativity.
rubric.how: State fluorine.

modelAnswer: Francium has the least value of ionization energy.
Fluorine has the highest value of electronegativity.

examTips: A short-answer question may ask you to compare metallic character or reactivity down a group or across a period. State the trend and give the electron-loss reason.
For a question about an element's position, use the group and period to infer whether it is metallic, electropositive, and likely to form a basic oxide.
In an explanation, earn marks by giving both the trend and the reason: for example, decreasing ionization energy makes electron loss easier.
If asked about density, give the unit g/cm³ and describe the trends as general ones; the listed values do not rise at every single step.

hints: Use the group and period to decide whether barium is a metal.
Then connect metals with electron loss, basic oxides, and the usual physical state of metals.

explain.title: Meaning of metallic character
explain.body: The metallic character is the tendency of an element to lose electrons and form positive ions or cations. An element that loses electrons readily has strong metallic character.

explain.title: Trend down a group
explain.body: Since the ionization energy decreases down the group, the elements have increased ability to lose electrons. For this reason both the metallic character and reactivity increase down the group.

explain.title: Trend across a period
explain.body: As we move from left to right in a period, the nuclear charge increases due to a gradual increase in the number of protons in the nucleus. Owing to this the valence electrons are pulled strongly by the nucleus making it difficult for the atoms to lose electrons. Hence the metallic character decreases in a period from left to right.

explain.title: Reactivity across a period and density
explain.body: The chemical reactivity gradually decreases as we move from left to right in a period through the metals, because losing electrons becomes more difficult. Moving further right towards non-metals, chemical reactivity gradually increases again. Density is mass per unit volume, is expressed in g/cm³, and generally increases down a group.

mistakes: Do not say metallic character increases from left to right; it decreases across a period.
Do not forget the reason for the trend: ionization energy decreases down a group, so losing electrons becomes easier.
Do not treat the reactivity trend across a whole period as a simple continuous decrease; it increases again towards non-metals.
Do not claim density rises at every step in the displayed Group 1 data; describe the trend as general.
Do not confuse electropositive (tendency to lose electrons) with electronegative (tendency to attract electrons).
